BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Threshold point: the "FINAL / STANDARD" framing

The Seller's package says the positions were "settled at principal level" and "marked FINAL", and that [STANDARD] clauses need no scrutiny. We shouldn't accept any of that:

- **Our playbook doesn't support it.** Nothing in it shows these positions were agreed, and every [STANDARD] item departs from it. Please confirm with Amelia Frost whether she agreed anything at principal level. Until she confirms in writing, treat the claim as unverified.
- **The labels are the Seller's, and the market statements are their assertions.** I reviewed every clause regardless of its label, and the issues below sit almost entirely under [STANDARD] tags.
- **Several of their figures match our fallbacks.** The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month period are the fallbacks that need Amelia's written authority, and none has been given. We shouldn't accept them, signal flexibility, or reveal that fallbacks exist.

## Material issues

### A. Liability architecture (most serious)

| Item | Seller | Our position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m | Needs written authority we don't have. Reject. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | Roughly 5x higher and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined with the de minimis, many small-to-mid claims would be unrecoverable. |
| General period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | Fallback needing approval, not given. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. "Administrative simplicity" would cap title at 20% for 18 months, which defeats the purpose of title warranties. |
| Limitation scope (12.3/13) | Limits apply to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise | Separate categories, no hidden general override | Reverses the default, so every special category (title, tax, IP, indemnities) would be swept in unless expressly excluded. |
| Fraud (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | The most serious point, and nobody can waive it. "Any nature" would capture fraud, so a carve-out must be added. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Disclosure (Schedule 7, Letter 1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records against the warranties. This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure we reject. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties.
- **Buyer knowledge (8.3).** It bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, **including anything "discoverable"** from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge on top of deemed disclosure, and it would neutralise much of the warranty package. Delete it. If a fallback qualifier is ever considered, it needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and it can never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Letter para 11.** It puts the burden on the Buyer to "evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement". Read with 8.3, it supports the Seller later arguing we knew. We should not acknowledge it as a basis for knowledge or disclosure.
- **Letter 1.4.** The non-admission language is acceptable only if it doesn't dilute warranties or indemnities. Make that explicit.

### C. Completion mechanics

- **Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Letter para 2 admits there is no consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. We need a condition precedent requiring effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer of this weight, and consent-on-delivery could leave us with a consent that is conditional or ineffective.
- **Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m).** The Seller offers a post-Completion release. Letter para 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and there is no discharge. Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion, consistent with debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release is possible only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia's approval, and neither exists. Also check change-control clause 8.1 for any trigger on the sale.
- **Bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000).** The Seller calls them "a matter for the Seller" and leaves them out of the funds flow. The Letter (para 5) confirms they're excluded and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs. Require a specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding, covering the on-costs triggered by payment. Don't assume a figure for the on-costs until payroll advice confirms it. Otherwise the Company bears the cost after Completion, which erodes the price.

### D. Specific matters

- **Ironquay IP (180,000).** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, which is too narrow. Broaden it to cover IP ownership, third-party claims and related costs, and preserve the SOW3 cure (payment of every SOW3 fee under clause 7.3, followed by transfer of the Project Materials). The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way, since DD-010 isn't bank verification and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. Don't treat it as confirmed owing or confirmed paid. Ask for payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.
- **DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an unsupported characterisation, and we shouldn't accept it. We also shouldn't overreach: the Letter itself says the investigation is preliminary, with no confirmed access, scope or notification duty. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Ask for log preservation, a proper investigation, regular updates and cooperation covenants, and reserve rights. Don't propose a price figure or a concession.
- **Sandbar (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls these ordinary course, but the Letter (para 8) says it doesn't state whether they're unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Don't accept that characterisation, and don't treat them as Debt or deduct from the price automatically. Request the contracts, term and termination rights, accrual status and timing, then assess.
- **Tax and IP.** The Seller says the positions are "settled under the general regime". They are not. Keep them open and separate from the general regime, with no hidden override. Don't propose unlimited liability or treat the positions as resolved.
- **Title.** The Seller relies on the DD-012 register. It is a supplied internal source, not independent proof, and Letter para 10 concedes we haven't verified it. Require independent evidence: share certificates and transfer history, ASIC and encumbrance/PPSR searches, board and shareholder authority, Seller capacity, and a clean-title warranty in the fundamental regime. Searching public registers for verification doesn't mean we accept them as deemed disclosure.

### E. Lower priority

- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** Both disclosures say consent isn't expressly required for a share sale. Verify against the underlying documents. Ensure any lease notification obligation is covered by a Seller covenant. This is a diligence follow-up rather than a playbook departure.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Don't treat anything as agreed.** Confirm with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level agreement exists. Reject the "FINAL" and "[STANDARD]" framing in writing and say all clauses remain under review.
2. **Hold the playbook positions:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket; 24 months. Don't concede the 20% cap or 18 months, since both need Amelia's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Build a separate fundamental/title regime:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reverse the "limits apply to all Claims" default.
4. **Insert the fraud carve-out** (fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct) across all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.
5. **Replace the general disclosure** with specific fair disclosure, and delete clause 8.3 buyer knowledge.
6. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark real Completion requirements:** effective Bluefen consent plus evidence its conditions are met; Riverlark payout from Completion funds with effective releases.
7. **Require a specific line item or Seller funding for the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs.**
8. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** while preserving the SOW3 cure, and get payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.
9. **Handle DD-006 neutrally:** preservation, investigation and update covenants, without conceding the Seller's "not material" label or asserting a breach.
10. **Request Sandbar documents** and assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
11. **Keep tax and IP open and separate,** with no deemed settlement under the general regime.
12. **Require independent title evidence** beyond DD-012.
13. **Verify the lease and Mossvale terms** against the underlying documents.

I can draft a mark-up or a response letter to the Seller's counsel next. It would state our positions without referring to the fallbacks.
